parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/users/domain/user.ts is declared as a domain file, but it does work that belongs to other layers. When the module loads, it reads the database configuration (databaseConfig().isDocumentDatabase) to choose the id type, which is a persistence/infrastructure concern. Every field also carries Swagger @ApiProperty metadata, which is transport/API documentation for the presentation layer. It also uses class-transformer @Expose/@Exclude with response groups ('me', 'admin'), which is presentation logic: it decides which fields go into API responses for each audience. A domain entity should hold domain state and rules without depending on the database driver or HTTP serialization.

violations.message: The module-level `idType` statement calls databaseConfig() and branches on isDocumentDatabase. This puts persistence/infrastructure configuration logic in the domain entity.
The User class fields carry @ApiProperty Swagger decorators, which are presentation/transport API-documentation metadata, inside the domain layer.

The User class uses class-transformer @Expose({ groups: ['me','admin'] }) and @Exclude({ toPlainOnly: true }) to control response serialization. This is a presentation concern inside the domain entity.
